name: Antimatter: CPT tests, antihydrogen spectroscopy and antimatter gravity
observables: antiproton and proton magnetic moments and charge-to-mass ratios
gravitational acceleration of antihydrogen and antiprotons
antihydrogen production, trapping times and numbers
overview: Antimatter experiments compare antiparticles and anti-atoms with their matter counterparts, testing charge-parity-time (CPT) invariance and the weak equivalence principle for antimatter. At CERN’s Antiproton Decelerator (AD), which produces low-energy antiprotons for studies of antimatter and “creates” antiatoms, and its ELENA ring, antiprotons are either confined in Penning traps and compared directly with the proton, or combined with positrons to make antihydrogen. ALPHA observed the 1S–2S transition in trapped antihydrogen at a frequency consistent with that expected for hydrogen; BASE measured the antiproton magnetic moment at the parts-per-billion level, consistent with the proton’s; and ALPHA-g found that released antihydrogen atoms fall towards Earth like ordinary matter. None of these measurements has found a matter–antimatter difference.
question: Do matter and antimatter obey exactly the same laws: the same masses, magnetic moments and atomic spectra, and the same response to gravity?

name: Neutron physics: EDM, lifetime and decay correlations
observables: neutron decay correlation coefficients (a, b, A, B, C) and the CKM element Vud
neutron gravitational quantum states and short-range gravity limits
overview: Free-neutron experiments at reactors, spallation sources and ultracold-neutron (UCN) sources probe the Standard Model at low energy. Dubbers and Schmidt note that experiments with cold and ultracold neutrons have reached a precision at which problems beyond the Standard Model become accessible to experimental investigation, with neutron decay measurements, the neutron electric dipole moment and baryogenesis among the linked questions. A permanent neutron EDM would signal time-reversal violation and, assuming CPT symmetry, CP violation; the nEDM experiment at PSI measured d_n = (0.0 ± 1.1 stat ± 0.2 sys) × 10⁻²⁶ e cm, consistent with zero. The UCNτ experiment at Los Alamos measured the free-neutron lifetime as 877.75 ± 0.28 (stat) +0.22/−0.16 (syst) s, a precision at which lifetime measurements address refinements in the Standard Model description of neutron decay.
question: How long does a free neutron live, how exactly does it decay, and does it carry a permanent electric dipole moment that would violate time-reversal symmetry?
